title: Cliff Booth Rides Again: Brad Pitt, Fincher and Tarantino Light Up the L.A. World Premiere
excerpt: Brad Pitt returned as Cliff Booth at Monday's Los Angeles world premiere, with director David Fincher and writer Quentin Tarantino beside him. IMAX opens Nov. 25.
content:
Brad Pitt walked the red carpet at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Hollywood on Monday night, November 16, for the world premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, returning to the role that won him an Academy Award — and bringing two of Hollywood’s biggest names with him.

Pitt, 62, was joined on the carpet by his girlfriend, jewelry designer Ines de Ramon, 33. The couple, who have been romantically linked since 2022, walked the premiere together holding hands, according to People.

The film is a standalone sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s 2019 Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, which grossed $410 million worldwide. Tarantino wrote the sequel’s screenplay but handed directing duties to David Fincher — a pairing that made Monday night one of the most closely watched premieres of the year.

A different Hollywood, 1977

The story picks up in 1977, eight years after the events of the original film. The official synopsis: “Brad Pitt returns to his Academy Award-winning role as Cliff Booth, only this time it’s 1977 and it’s a very different Hollywood.” The stuntman-turned-drifter faces what early reports describe as “murder, blackmail, theft and extortion.”

The red carpet drew the film’s ensemble: Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Carla Gugino, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian and Timothy Olyphant, alongside Fincher and Tarantino.

First reactions: “wild” and “effortlessly perfect”

Audiences at the premiere were quick to share first impressions online, with early reactions calling the film “wild” and “effortlessly perfect.” One awards-season writer described it as a “wild, hilarious hangout movie.” Full reviews remain under embargo until November 19.

A release plan unlike any Netflix has tried

The film’s rollout is the most unusual in Netflix history. It opens November 25 in an exclusive two-week IMAX engagement — a first for the streamer — before arriving on Netflix on December 23. The two-week theatrical window puts a Netflix film on the biggest screens of the holiday season before it ever reaches a living room.

The project began as an unproduced Tarantino script of about 230 pages, which Netflix acquired in 2025. Fincher trimmed roughly 60 pages from the draft before filming.

What it means

Analysis: Monday night was about more than a premiere — it was Netflix betting that a theatrical event can still move the needle for a streaming release. Pairing Pitt’s most beloved character with Tarantino’s words and Fincher’s direction is the strongest hand the company has played all year, and the early reactions suggest the gamble may pay off. The real test comes November 25, when audiences — not just the premiere crowd — decide whether Cliff Booth still has the pull he had in 2019. If the IMAX run sells out, expect every streamer to start rethinking what a “Netflix movie” is allowed to be.
